topic: Longitudinal event and work-item state transitions in dialogue and operational communication, with emphasis on supersession, correction, contradiction, reopening, source-relative factuality, evidential confirmation, and preservation of historical state.
executive_summary: The corpus establishes several complementary foundations for longitudinal state reasoning but does not evaluate them as one integrated operational-communication task. Factuality work shows that event status is source-relative and distinct from objective verification, while temporal-relation research demonstrates useful ordering models and global consistency mechanisms. Commitment and dialogue formalisms distinguish lifecycle transitions, retraction, correction, persistence, and reopening. Belief-revision research separately distinguishes changed-world updates from corrected beliefs and offers conflict-preserving revision strategies. Temporal-database, provenance, and event-sourcing work provides mechanisms for retaining historical states and derivations. Important empirical tensions remain over the value of transitivity and alternative timeline representations. Most NLP evidence is news-derived, while lifecycle and revision evidence is mainly formal, modeled, or adjacent-domain. None of the eight prior gaps is fully resolved by the expanded corpus.
themes: Source-relative factuality and attribution are distinct from independent verification of real-world completion.

Temporal ordering benefits from structured representations, contextual knowledge, and sometimes global consistency inference, but the measured contribution of particular constraints is architecture- and dataset-dependent.
Commitment and dialogue models provide explicit semantics for cancellation, violation, correction, retraction, persistence, and reopening.

Belief change distinguishes changes in the world from corrections to information about the world and offers multiple strategies for resolving inconsistency without simply deleting all conflicting information.
Temporal databases, provenance theory, and event-sourcing practice provide complementary accounts of historical-state retention, temporal dimensions, derivation lineage, and schema evolution.
The admitted literature validates individual components in different domains; their combination into longitudinal workplace work-item tracking remains untested.

findings.statement: Event factuality is represented in the admitted factuality literature as a source's commitment or presentation regarding an event rather than as direct proof of objective real-world truth; FactBank further demonstrates that source identification and factuality value can be annotated with substantial inter-annotator agreement.

Factuality can vary across mentions or sources: FactBank preserves source-relative assessments, while document-level ExDLEF explicitly observes differing sentence-level factualities for one event but predicts a single document-level value, thereby demonstrating two different factuality representations rather than a longitudinal revision model.

Temporal-relation extraction on news-derived benchmarks improves when models incorporate temporal commonsense, structured representations, relative-time signals, or global inference, although the contribution of specific global constraints varies substantially across experiments.

Formal commitment models distinguish lifecycle outcomes that would be conflated by a single active/inactive status: cancellation is different from violation, conditional commitments can detach or expire, and commitment state can be updated incrementally as new events are processed.

Dialogue theories in the corpus treat correction and retraction as changes to current commitments rather than erasure of earlier utterances; they also model preservation of undenied prior material and, in correction-of-correction cases, restoration of previously displaced commitments.

The belief-change literature distinguishes update caused by a changed world from revision caused by new information about a world treated as static, while disjunctive revision demonstrates that conflicts in prioritized propositional knowledge bases can be weakened rather than wholly discarded, retaining consequences that deletion-based alternatives lose.

Temporal-database work argues that event time, valid time, and transaction time jointly preserve histories involving retroactive updates, proactive updates, corrections, and delayed recording, while database provenance theory separately distinguishes why an output exists from where its values originated.

Industrial event-sourcing evidence shows that retention of state changes is an audit rationale and identifies several schema-evolution techniques, including techniques that preserve original source events, but the same study also reports that complete immutability and complete audit history were not universal among the systems examined.

Adjacent-domain multi-source fact verification benefits on the reported Check-COVID and FEVEROUS-S benchmarks from retaining different evidence-source roles in a heterogeneous graph, but this result evaluates claim verification rather than longitudinal lifecycle transitions or workplace-message state tracking.

Cross-document news timeline construction benefits from combining temporal and semantic compatibility, and the reported manual-coreference experiment shows that upstream entity-coreference errors materially limit downstream event recall; this evidence concerns event identity and ordering, not revision of an event's factual or workflow state.

contradictions.topic: Measured value of global temporal transitivity
contradictions.note: CAEVO reports a large gain when transitive inference is added in its dense temporal-ordering setup, whereas the structured joint model reports no gain from the transitivity constraint on TB-Dense and only 0.1 F1 on MATRES. These results should not be averaged into a universal conclusion because the architectures, inference mechanisms, candidate graphs, and evaluation settings differ.

contradictions.topic: Direct timeline prediction versus indirect relation-to-timeline conversion
contradictions.note: Within the same study, contextual direct timeline prediction outperforms TL2RTL on the TE3 split, while TL2RTL outperforms the direct model on the smaller TimeBank-Dense-derived split. The paper attributes part of this reversal to dataset size, density, and class-balance differences.

contradictions.topic: Single document-level factuality versus preservation of source- or mention-relative assessments
contradictions.note: ExDLEF defines one document-level factuality value even when local sentence-level values differ, whereas FactBank-based work explicitly models factuality relative to sources. This is a representational tension rather than evidence that either task definition is universally superior.

The paper's narrative claim that DLGRN has fewer parameters than all baselines conflicts with its own tables, which list BERT at 109.5M parameters and DLGRN at 119.7M. This internal inconsistency does not invalidate its reported factuality scores but weakens the parameter-efficiency claim.

gaps.description: No admitted paper directly evaluates longitudinal state tracking across workplace messages in which one work item moves among requested, proposed, planned, approved, completed, revoked, superseded, disputed, conditional, and unresolved states while retaining historical assessments.
gaps.suggested_query: longitudinal event state tracking dialogue email requested planned approved completed revoked superseded

gaps.description: The corpus provides formal treatments of correction, retraction, persistence, and reopening, but does not establish a natural-language method evaluated across successive operational communications for distinguishing supersession, correction, supplementation, contradiction, reopening, and unresolved conflict.
gaps.suggested_query: natural language supersession correction contradiction revision reopening dialogue event state

gaps.description: No admitted paper jointly evaluates source-relative factuality, temporal ordering, lifecycle state, contradiction, and provenance as one longitudinal model; the papers validate separate components and their combination remains untested.
gaps.suggested_query: "event factuality" temporal relation contradiction provenance longitudinal state tracking

gaps.description: Direct evidence for workplace email, Teams-like dialogue, or comparable operational communication is absent; the empirical NLP evidence is predominantly news-derived, while the commitment and belief-revision papers use formal, modeled, argumentative-dialogue, or adjacent-domain settings.
gaps.suggested_query: workplace email dialogue event factuality temporal revision commitment status tracking

gaps.description: The admitted factuality literature models textual source commitment, and the fact-verification paper models heterogeneous corroborating evidence, but no admitted paper establishes how to distinguish an author's assertion that work is complete from independent confirmation or stronger evidential verification of completion in longitudinal operational communication.
gaps.suggested_query: event factuality evidentiality source attribution independent confirmation verification reported completion

gaps.description: Evaluation is still needed on adversarial longitudinal sequences such as plan-to-cancel, approve-to-revoke, deadline changes, contradictory same-time updates, out-of-order ingestion, stale messages arriving late, and completion claims later corrected.

The combined representation of message time, event/effective time, deadline or constraint time, and observed collection/version time has not been benchmarked for this product's state-resolution tasks; the temporal-database paper provides a related three-time formal account rather than such an evaluation.

The corpus does not evaluate a provenance-preserving implementation for this state-resolution task that stores immutable source observations and successive assessments while exposing a separately derived current-state view.

actionable_insights: Synthesis-derived recommendation: represent source observations, source-relative assessments, and any derived current-state assessment as distinct records rather than collapsing them into one mutable fact. This is a project decision inferred from the combined literature, not a configuration directly evaluated by the papers.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: model correction, supersession, contradiction, supplementation, reopening, and unresolved conflict as distinct candidate relations and test them independently before allowing any relation to replace prior state. This combined taxonomy is a project decision; no admitted paper evaluates it end to end.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: keep temporal ordering and factuality or lifecycle status as separate dimensions so that an event can be temporally positioned without being treated as factual or completed. The exact product representation is a project decision.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: maintain separate source-relative claims when parties disagree and derive any consolidated assessment from those claims with explicit provenance. The consolidation policy is a project decision and is not validated by the cited dialogue or factuality experiments.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: build an engineering benchmark around adversarial state-transition sequences, including late-arriving evidence and corrections of corrections, because the admitted literature does not provide an equivalent workplace benchmark.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: evaluate global temporal constraints empirically rather than assuming they will help; the admitted experiments show materially different effects across architectures and datasets.

Synthesis-derived recommendation: treat independent confirmation as an evidential dimension separate from linguistic factuality until targeted literature or product-specific evaluation establishes a justified mapping between them.
confidence_summary: Confidence is high in the component-level conclusions concerning source-relative factuality, temporal-relation modeling, formal commitment-state transitions, correction and retraction semantics, and the existence of history-preserving provenance or event-sourcing mechanisms. Confidence is medium for transfer from those results to longitudinal workplace communication because most quantitative NLP evidence is news-derived and several relevant papers are formal, conceptual, modeled, or adjacent-domain rather than production-email studies. The corpus therefore supports well-supported design principles and testable mechanisms, but it does not provide direct empirical validation of their integration into one longitudinal work-item state model.
limitations: The corpus contains no direct benchmark of longitudinal workplace email or Teams-like communication covering the target lifecycle states.
Most empirical temporal and factuality NLP results come from news-derived corpora; transfer to operational communication is untested.
Several important lifecycle, correction, retraction, belief-change, and provenance results are formal or conceptual rather than corpus-scale empirical evaluations.

The temporal-database paper doi-10-1016-0020-0255-94-90059-0, the update-versus-revision paper doi-10-1017-cbo9780511526664-007, and HeterMV doi-10-1016-j-ipm-2026-104709 were available only at abstract or preview level in the supplied analyses, limiting inspection of detailed methods and failure cases.

Papers separately validate factuality, temporal ordering, commitment transitions, provenance, belief revision, and multi-source verification; the corpus contains no experiment validating their combined use as one scheme.
The admitted work does not establish a general rule for deciding when a later communication supersedes rather than merely contradicts, supplements, or corrects an earlier one.
The source-relative factuality literature concerns what sources commit to in text and does not by itself establish independent real-world confirmation.
The DLGRN paper contains an internal inconsistency between its parameter-efficiency prose claim and its reported parameter tables.
Inherited Topic 05 handoffs and project context were used only to scope relevance; they were not treated as evidence for findings or gap closure.

gap_status.note: Commitment lifecycle and dialogue papers model several individual transitions, but no paper evaluates the full longitudinal workplace-state inventory while retaining historical assessments.

Correction, retraction, persistence, and reopening receive formal treatment, but the complete distinction among supersession, correction, supplementation, contradiction, reopening, and unresolved conflict is not evaluated as a natural-language longitudinal classification problem.

The corpus contains evidence for each of several components, but no admitted experiment combines source-relative factuality, temporal ordering, lifecycle state, contradiction handling, and provenance in one longitudinal model.
The new papers remain news-derived, formal, modeled, argumentative-dialogue, event-sourcing, database, or fact-verification evidence rather than direct workplace operational-communication evaluation.

HeterMV adds multi-source corroboration evidence, but neither it nor the factuality papers evaluates the specific distinction between a work-completion assertion and independent confirmation of that completion in longitudinal workplace communication.
Individual papers cover cancellation, violation, correction, retraction, temporal ordering, and retroactive updates, but none supplies the specified adversarial longitudinal benchmark.

The temporal-database paper formally distinguishes event, valid, and transaction times, but the requested four-way product representation including message time, deadline/constraint time, and observed collection/version time has not been benchmarked for state resolution.

Provenance theory and event-sourcing practice establish relevant historical-retention mechanisms, but no admitted paper evaluates the specified immutable-observation plus successive-assessment plus derived-current-view implementation for this task.
